To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have developed a protocol to fabricate laminin and RBM-polycaprolactic acid (PCL) nanofibers and that laminin-PCL nanofibers maintain embryonic stem cell pluripotency and RBM-PPL nanofibers support neurite outgrowth.

we have successfully developed laminin and RBM-Poly (ε-caprolactone) nanofibrous scaffolds that mimic the structure and composition of the basement membrane and have shown that they can be used to promote cell attachment, proliferation, and maintenance of pluripotency in stem cells.

laminin- and reconstituted-basement membrane-polycaprlactone (PCLA) blend nanofibres are a suitable scaffold to maintain the undifferentiated state of embryonic stem cells and to promote neurite outgrowth in PC12 cells.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and characterization of novel biomaterials and tissue engineering strategies to promote the regeneration of damaged tissues.
the development of a novel, electrospun, nanoscale scaffold that is biocompatible and mimics the basement membrane (a thin, extracellular matrix layer) that surrounds all tissues.
the development of a biomimetic scaffold for regenerative applications.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
laminin and basement membrane-PCL scaffolds are promising biomimetic substrates for regenerative medicine.

the use of laminin-PCL and RBM-PCLS scaffolds as biomimetic scaffolds in the field of regenerative medicine has shown great promise in terms of maintaining the undifferentiated state of human embryonic stem cell colonies, as well as promoting the attachment, neurite outgrowth and viability of PC12 cells in vitro.
the use of electrospun NFs as a scaffold for stem cell culture is a promising approach to regenerative medicine.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
laminin and reconstituted BM-PCL NFs can be used as biomimetic scaffolds in regenerative medicine.

laminin-PCL and reconstituted RBM-PCL nanofiber scaffolds are a promising biomimic for regenerative medicine, and that laminin-PDL nanofibers may be useful for maintaining undifferentiated human ES cell colonies.
we have developed a protocol for electro-spinning laminin and basement membrane-polylactic acid nanofibers and evaluated them as scaffolds for regenerative medicine.
The main takeaway from our work is that
electrospun laminins and RBM-PCLS are promising scaffolds for regenerative medicine.
we can use electrospinning to mimic basement membranes and that this can be useful for tissue engineering applications.
laminin and reconstituted BM can be used to make nanofibrous matrices that can be used as scaffolds for tissue engineering.
